title: From almost tight $p$-group enumeration to $2$-group domination among finite groups
summary: Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. The pioneering works of Higman (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) and Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965), with improvement by Newman and Seeley, establish that \[ \frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac{4}{9}m^2+Ω(m)\leq \log_p f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3+O(m^{5/2}). \] In the same paper in 1965, Sims speculated on improving the error term ($O(m^{8/3})$ at that time) in the upper bound. To show that $f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3+O(m^2)$ is now known as Sims' conjecture. Our first main result proves Sims' conjecture in a strong…
